newsitem.title: INDIA: Two India ITC officials placed in custody.
newsitem.headline: Two India ITC officials placed in custody.

text.p: An Indian court on Tuesday rejected the bail plea of two directors of ITC Ltd and remanded them in judicial custody for alleged violations of foreign exchange rules until December 3.
ITC executive director R.P. Agarwal and P.K. Talwar, finance director of ITC Bhadrachalam, a paper and packaging firm affiliated with ITC, were arrested by the Enforcement Directorate on Monday.

Calcutta's chief metropolitan magistrate, A.K. Dasgupta, rejected their bail plea. "The two officials have been accused of under-invoicing of imports of machinery to the tune of $1 million, violating foreign exchange rules," he said.
"To facilitate further investigation, the two accused have been sent to judicial custody till December three," Dasgupta said.
Earlier, Enforcement Directorate deputy director K.K. Kabirpanthi told Reuters that the two executives had been arrested "for their involvement in violation of foreign exchange rules".
Agarwal denied allegations that he had broken foreign exchange rules.
"This is a matter of sub judice," Agarwal told reporters as police escorted him to a local police station on Monday. "I cannot say anything. But I don't agree with any of their allegations."

With Monday's arrests, 12 people have been detained in the case which broke into public view last month when the Enforcement Directorate launched nationwide raids into homes and offices of ITC officials.
Among those arrested were two former ITC chairmen and several serving or retired senior executives.
The Enforcement Directorate is an arm of the Finance Ministry, which has said the violations involved up to $100 million in ITC's international operations.
